Roping in a cyclone occurs when the underflow discharge from the spigot collapses into a solid stream instead of a hollow cone. This happens when the flare angle decreases and the air core cannot maintain the flow, causing the underflow to become denser and solid. The cause is using a spigot that is too small, preventing the air core from operating efficiently. [2]
